recipes.name: Slow Cooker Thai Pork with Peppers
ingredients_raw: 2 red bell peppers, thinly sliced and cut into bite-size lengths

steps.text: Combine bell peppers, chicken broth, soy sauce, peanut butter, garlic, honey, ginger, and pepper flakes in a slow cooker; add pork, turning to coat.
Cover the slow cooker. Cook on Low until pork is tender, 5 to 6 hours.
Transfer pork from sauce to a cutting board using a slotted spoon. Shred pork; return to sauce in the slow cooker. Cook until hot, about 10 minutes; serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Thai Pork with Peppers
raw_recipe.description: This slow-cooker Thai pork with peppers recipe simmers pork and peppers in a Thai peanut sauce until aromatic and tender. Serve it over jasmine rice.

review.reviewBody: This was a very tasty and EASY recipe. Didn't change a thing as a true review should be in my opinion and we LOVED it over rice. Even better 2 days later when I mixed the pork mixture with the rice and warmed it up in a skillet.

Cut the honey a bit. Melted the PB with the other ingredients 1st. Put carrots and pork and cooked on low 2 hours. Added lots of broccoli, cooked for another hour 20 min, then added the peppers and zucchini. I wanted to beef it up with lots of veggies and will do this again next time but will double the sauce.

Yummy served atop Jasmine rice....don't shred the meat! Cut boneless chops into strips and don't add the bell peppers until the last half-hour of cooking or they will disintegrate. I also cut the ginger in half...way too much for only 1 lb. of meat, and although I LOVE garlic, some of my cloves were pretty big so I only used 4, which I thought gave it plenty of garlic flavor. Sprinkled some fresh chopped cilantro on top & a squeeze of fresh lime, too. Enjoy with an ice cold beer! :-)

Excellent. I don’t have a slow cooker so I cooked it on low heat on the stove for 2 hours, and I had to add more water in the middle. I added roasted broccoli when it was done and served over brown rice.

This was a very easy recipe to get together with ingredients that I keep in my pantry. I added the peppers to the slow cooker about half way into the cooking and they were still a little softer than I would have liked. I also thought the sauce was too thin, so, I removed the pork, added a cornstarch slurry, & brought the liquid to a boil to thicken the sauce. I then added the pork back to the sauce to warm through. I topped with some fresh green onion for a little crunch. Both my husband and I liked the flavor of the dish, but, thought the flavor profile was missing something. Perhaps a little fresh cilantro? Overall we thought it was a pretty good recipe and I would make it again.

This was a very tasty dish although very spicey. Made exactly as written except only had one red pepper and followed other suggestions to put peppers in recipe later. Also had 1 1/2 pounds of boneless pork chops frozen together so when thawed used all. The house smelled heavenly while cooking. Did 8 hours on low, added peppers four hours in, shredded pork and returned to sauce at 7 hours. Served over rice. Next time, I would double the sauce (except red pepper flakes as dish was quite hot), and make sure I have two red peppers.

I really like how the sauce tastes. I usually use pork tenderloin. I doubled the crushed red pepper flakes to become a little bit more hot. As other reviews say: just put the bell peppers (which I used half red and half green) in the last hour, otherwise it become too much softened and not good. I also added some sliced mushrooms by the last half hour.
I cubed the pork before putting in slow cooker, and waited to add the vegetables so they did not get soggy. It was great served over noodles, and you may want to make extra sauce as well!

Very good, very satisfying. I did veer from the recipe: I did not use chicken broth but instead subbed a can of coconut milk. Did not use honey, but brown sugar. I did not put the peppers in the slow cooker but rather mixed them with olive oil, lemon juice, salt and then broiled them (with onions) to vary the texture.

12/16: R&S, K,A,D,R. Everyone loved. Deven had 2nds! Excellent sauce, tripled amount and had enough left to use for another meal(will try over noodles). Sauce creamy, not soupy. Used 2 pork loins instead of chops. Cooked one in slow cooker which was a bit shredded when sliced. The other one baked in oven, sliced nicely and put into sauce in slow cooker. Wouldn't recommend shredding. May need to cook less to prevent shredding upon slicing, 4-5hrs instead of 5-6 on low. Served sliced with sauce and butternut barley risotto as a side. Next time may use crunchy peanut butter, and serve with brown or Thai Jasmine rice. Definitely will garnish with finely chopped peanuts and sliced scallions. Also per reviews could add other veggies such as broccoli florets.

Now that is delicious! I cut the garlic to 3 cloves and added the bell pepper plus some red onion in the last 30 minutes, along wit 1 tbsp of cornstarch to thicken it a little (turned up to high). Mine was done in about 4 1/2 hours on low. I also used 1 tsp of ground ginger instead of ginger root.

Very good! I did change it up a bit. I used boneless ribs cut into cubes 1-2 inches in size, shook them in a bag with flour and salt and pepper, browned them well then set aside. Sauted onion, garlic and peppers then added the pork and remaining ingredients and simmered on the stove top for about 1 hour stirring often.

Family like it. Next time use more pepper flakes. I did make any changes other than I used a little bit more of the peanut butter, honey and soy sauce after I tasted the sauce. I also used cornstarch to thicken it and served it over rice.
I found this to be surprisingly bland. I added peanuts at the end, and some extra red pepper flakes, but all in all, in was meh.
Made no changes except did not shed the meat. It was soft and crumbly as it was.Delicious!
One of our favorites. I have made several times!

Other than using cubed pork shoulder - so skipped the shredding. Otherwise, made exactly as written and we found this amazing! A little heat but subtle enough for my spice-sensitive husband. Topped with peanuts and served over quinoa- which may seem odd but it actually enhanced textures even more. A crockpot keeper for sure! Thank you!!
Family favorite and super easy.

I made this with plenty of bell peppers and it came out fantastic!!! I doubled the recipe BUT accidentally forgot the chicken stock and it still came out great. I think I’ll keep it out again next time because it was perfect.
I’ve made this before and rated it previously too. This recipe never fails and any left over juice is great with rice!
